evidence.quote: The API can be accessed by creating a Personal Access Token from the Developers section of Harvest ID.
Personal Access Tokens replace the Basic Authentication method that was used in our v1 API, as this is more secure.
because it's more secure and the access token is never visible by a browser

result.notes: Free "$0 forever" 1-seat plan lets any developer sign up and mint a Personal Access Token (bearer token) from Harvest ID's Developers section without sales contact; OAuth2 (Authorization Code + Implicit) is documented for multi-user apps. Basic auth was used in v1 but has been replaced by PATs in v2, so it is not listed as a current method. api_breadth is an estimate (medium) based on ~13 documented resource categories (Clients, Invoices, Estimates, Expenses, Tasks, Timesheets, Projects, Roles, Users, Reports, PTO) since no exact endpoint count was published. No official vendor MCP server found; several community MCP servers exist on GitHub (e.g. ianaleck/harvest-mcp-server, taiste/harvest-mcp-server) per registry leads, not independently verified by fetch.
result.one_liner: Harvest is a time-tracking, invoicing, and expense-management app for freelancers and teams with a REST API v2.
